metadata.title: The Fall That Stops Speeding Up
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: A skydiver jumps from a plane. Why does the diver eventually stop speeding up?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A skydiver jumps from a plane. Gravity pulls straight down with constant force, and the diver keeps speeding up, and up, and up.
beats.new_visual_element: A slate stick figure falls from the top of the frame. A thick crimson arrow labeled F gravity points straight down from the figure, fixed length. Three faded trailing afterimages show the spacing between successive positions widening.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: falling figure with fixed-length downward gravity arrow, widening afterimage spacing showing increasing speed

beats.narration_text: But the air pushes back. Drag is not constant — it grows with the square of speed. The faster the diver falls, the harder the air resists, so this upward force keeps lengthening.
beats.new_visual_element: A teal upward arrow labeled F drag appears at the figure's center, starting very short. As afterimage spacing widens further, the arrow accumulates length in visible discrete steps, always shorter than the fixed red gravity arrow.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: falling figure with fixed crimson gravity arrow and a growing but still-shorter teal drag arrow, afterimage spacing still widening

beats.narration_text: Eventually drag grows to match gravity exactly. The net force drops to zero, though the diver is still falling, fast, at last with constant speed.
beats.new_visual_element: The teal drag arrow reaches the same length as the fixed crimson gravity arrow, both drawn along a shared dashed vertical guideline. A gold label F net equals zero fades in between them. Afterimage spacing becomes perfectly even.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: equal-length crimson and teal arrows locked along the guideline, F net = 0 label, evenly spaced afterimages showing constant speed

beats.narration_text: Zero acceleration does not mean zero speed. It means the two forces have finally balanced, and the object keeps falling at a fixed rate. That balanced, unchanging fall speed is called terminal velocity.
beats.new_visual_element: The figure continues falling with unchanging afterimage spacing at the bottom of the frame. Both matched arrows remain locked at equal length. Bold text stamps on screen: TERMINAL VELOCITY — a = 0, v = constant.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held state: even afterimage spacing, matched arrows, TERMINAL VELOCITY caption stamped on screen
